$comment: Recorded contract for the OSC eyevinn-ffmpeg-s3 ephemeral job: the create-job body fields, and — the load-bearing part for issue #1191 — exactly which of ffmpeg's two output streams reaches the job's log. This is NOT a byte-identical upstream snapshot: the service publishes no OpenAPI/JSON document for its job shape (the OSC catalog's get-service-schema returns only provisioning config, see docs/contracts/README.md), so every value below was read out of the service's own source at the pinned commit and is cited to file:line in `source.symbols`. The sha256 of each upstream blob read is recorded so a refresh can tell drift from a re-read.

Two jobs were created, polled to a terminal status, read back, and removed. The first-run 2026-10-14 'NOT ATTEMPTED' note is superseded for `sceneCutReadback.viaS3Object`; the other `requiresLiveRun: true` fields not exercised by that run remain unanswered (see `openQuestionsRequiringALiveRun`).

symbols.pins: The whole job: prepare(stagingDir) -> rewriteCmdString(cmdString) -> runFFmpeg(...) -> uploadResult(dest, ...). runFFmpeg THROWS before uploadResult is reached, so a non-zero ffmpeg exit means nothing is ever uploaded.

THE load-bearing symbol for issue #1191. `spawnSync(ffmpeg, args, { cwd: stagingDir })` is called with NO `stdio` option, so the default 'pipe' applies: ffmpeg's stderr is captured into a buffer, not inherited by the container. That buffer is written to the container log by exactly one statement — `console.error(stderr.toString())` at :232 — which is inside `if (status !== 0)` (:227) and inside its `else` branch (:231-232, i.e. only when spawn itself did not error). CONSEQUENCE: when ffmpeg exits 0, its stderr is DISCARDED and never appears in the job log. Everything `showinfo` prints (`pts_time=...`) and everything `-loglevel` controls goes to stderr, so a successful ffmpeg run carries no showinfo lines into the log.

The only things the job writes to stdout on a SUCCESSFUL run: `Output file: <dest>`, `Staging directory: <dir>`, `Actual command string: <cmd>`, `cmdString: <cmd>`, the per-S3-argument `Generating signed URL for ...` lines, and `Uploaded <dest>` / `Uploaded package to <dest>` / `Successfully synced HLS output to <dest>`. No ffmpeg output of any kind.

`try { await doFFmpeg(...) } catch (err) { console.log(err.message) }` — a thrown error is printed as a single line and NOT rethrown, and no non-zero exit code is set. The container therefore exits 0 whether ffmpeg succeeded or failed, which is the mechanism behind the already-logged friction that a job reaches `SuccessCriteriaMet` with no output (docs/osc-feedback/incoming-issue786-ffmpeg-s3-terminal-status-without-output.md gap 1). For #1191 it means `job.status` cannot be used to tell 'ffmpeg exited 0' from 'ffmpeg exited non-zero', so it cannot be used to tell 'log has no ffmpeg stderr' from 'log has all of it'.
`stripQuotes(args.join(' ')).trim()` — the job's `cmdLineArgs` string is reassembled from argv and one pair of enclosing double quotes is stripped, then re-split by splitCmdLineArgs.

Hand-rolled splitter: splits on unquoted spaces, treats `"` as a quote TOGGLE and REMOVES it, treats `\` as an escape, and gives single quotes NO special meaning (they survive into the argument). So `-vf "select='gt(scene,0.4)',showinfo"` arrives at ffmpeg as the single argument `select='gt(scene,0.4)',showinfo`, with the single quotes intact for libavfilter's own parser to strip. A filter string containing a SPACE must stay double-quoted or it will be split.

The output is the LAST argument that does not start with `-`, and an output is MANDATORY (`throw new Error('No output file specified in ffmpeg command')` at :97-99). For `... -f null -` the trailing `-` starts with `-` and is skipped, so the detected output is the literal string `null`.

`localOutputFile = join(stagingDir, path.basename(toUrl(output).pathname))` and then `actualCmdString = actualCmdString.replace(output, localOutputFile)` — a plain FIRST-OCCURRENCE substring replace on the whole command string. For `-f null -` this rewrites the FORMAT NAME: `-f null -` becomes `-f /usercontent/<jobid>/null -`, which is not a muxer name. This is why the existing probe runner's command (`-i <url> -f null -`, src/pipeline/osc-ffprobe.ts:45-47 (ffprobeCmdLine)) cannot end in a zero exit — and, via runFFmpeg :227-232, why its ffmpeg stderr reaches the log at all.

For an `s3://` dest whose path does NOT end in `/`: `readdir(stagingDir)` then `files.find(f => f === basename(dest.pathname))`, and ONLY that one file is `aws s3 cp`'d to the dest. A missing match throws `Output file <name> not found in staging directory`. CONSEQUENCE for the #1191 fallback: a sidecar written by ffmpeg's `metadata=print:file=<name>` filter is NOT uploaded by this branch; only the muxer's own output file is.

For an `s3://` dest whose path DOES end in `/`: `aws s3 cp --recursive <stagingDir> <new URL(dirname(dest.pathname), dest)>` — the entire staging directory is uploaded, so a `metadata=print:file=` sidecar WOULD be carried. Note the destination is `dirname()` of an already-trailing-slash path, i.e. one level ABOVE the prefix given (`s3://bucket/a/b/` uploads to `s3://bucket/a/`), and that ffmpeg still has to write its own output to `join(stagingDir, basename('/a/b/')) = <stagingDir>/b`.

symbols.symbol: aws s3 presign for s3:// inputs
symbols.pins: An `s3://bucket/key` INPUT is converted to a 6h presigned URL by the bundled aws-cli (`--endpoint-url $S3_ENDPOINT_URL` when set) before ffmpeg sees it. ffmpeg echoes its `-i` argument into stderr, so any captured log can contain a live SigV4 query string — which is what src/pipeline/osc-job-log.ts redactLogQueryStrings exists to strip.

alpine:3.19 with `apk add aws-cli` (:12) and `apk add ffmpeg` (:13); `VOLUME /usercontent` (:21); `ENV STAGING_DIR=/usercontent` (:22); ENTRYPOINT docker-entrypoint.sh (:24) -> `ffmpeg-s3 "$@"` (docker-entrypoint.sh:9-12). The ffmpeg build is Alpine's distro package (Dockerfile:13), NOT a pinned build — so which muxers/filters exist is an Alpine packaging property and is not pinned by this contract.

logs.routeSource: src/pipeline/osc-ffprobe.ts:156-158 — resolved from the service's apiUrl by @osaas/client-core getLogsForInstance(context, serviceId, name, sat); recorded there as confirmed against the live API. It is NOT /ffmpeg-s3job/:name/logs.
logs.returnTypeSource: @osaas/client-core/lib/core.d.ts:85 (both shapes normalised in src/pipeline/osc-job-log.ts captureJobLogs and src/pipeline/osc-ffprobe.ts)
logs.lifetime: readable only while the ephemeral instance still exists — getLogsForInstance is an instance call, so `finally { removeJob }` destroys the artefact (src/pipeline/osc-job-log.ts header, gap 3 of the #786 friction log)
logs.carriesFfmpegStderr: ONLY WHEN ffmpeg EXITED NON-ZERO. Then the whole captured stderr buffer is emitted in one console.error (src/ffmpeg.ts:232). When ffmpeg exits 0 the buffer is dropped and the log holds only the wrapper's own console.log lines.
logs.truncationNote: UNANSWERED. Whether the OSC job-log route truncates, pages, or ring-buffers a long log — and at what size — is a platform property with no published contract and was not measured. Our own callers additionally cap what they RETAIN: src/pipeline/osc-job-log.ts MAX_LOG_CHARS = 4000, keeping the LAST 4000 characters; src/pipeline/osc-ffprobe.ts applies no cap of its own.
logs.observedOnExitZero: 2026-10-28 live run: the string returned by getLogsForInstance held only the wrapper's own lines (see `sceneCutReadback.viaS3Object.liveRun`), no ffmpeg stderr. Consistent with `carriesFfmpegStderr` above. A non-zero exit was not exercised, so the stderr-on-failure claim is still from source only.

viaLogShowinfo.reason: showinfo writes `pts_time=` to stderr, and stderr reaches the log only on a non-zero ffmpeg exit (src/ffmpeg.ts:224-235). With this exact command the exit is in fact non-zero — but only because rewriteCmdString rewrites the muxer name `null` into a staging path (src/ffmpeg.ts:190), i.e. the lines are readable by accident of a bug, not by contract. An upstream fix to the output rewrite removes the cuts from the log without changing any field we send.
viaLogShowinfo.ifFfmpegExitedZero: no showinfo lines in the log at all

viaS3Object.verdict: CONFIRMED BY LIVE RUN (2026-10-28), with the one hard constraint above
viaS3Object.constraint: The uploaded object must be ffmpeg's OWN muxer output: the single-file S3 branch uploads only the file whose basename equals the dest basename (src/ffmpeg.ts:337-345). A `-vf ...,metadata=print:file=scenes.txt` sidecar is written into the staging dir (cwd = stagingDir, src/ffmpeg.ts:224-226) but is NOT uploaded by that branch. The recursive branch (src/ffmpeg.ts:318-335, dest path ending in `/`) does upload it, at the cost of uploading the whole staging dir one prefix level above the dest.
viaS3Object.alsoRequires: ffmpeg must exit 0, or uploadResult is never reached (src/ffmpeg.ts:28-29). So the command must be a well-formed real encode/mux, not `-f null -`.
viaS3Object.shapeThatFitsTheUploader: -i s3://<bucket>/<key> -an -fps_mode passthrough -vf "select='gt(scene,0.4)'" -f framemd5 s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/<id>.framemd5 — the framemd5 muxer's own output lines carry the per-selected-frame pts plus a `#tb` timebase header, so the cut list IS the output file and the single-file upload branch applies unchanged.

findings: THE TIMEBASE IS NOT FIXED. The `#tb 0:` header is the stream timebase of the source: `1/25` for the multi-segment clip, `1/12800` for the single-segment mp4. A parser MUST read `#tb` and compute seconds = pts * num / den; it must not assume 1/25 or any constant.
Row columns are `stream#, dts, pts, duration, size, hash`; the pts column is the third. Only frames selected by `select='gt(scene,0.4)'` appear.
The first frame of the stream is NOT listed as a cut. For the 12s clip with cuts at 3s, 6s and 9s the object has exactly three rows, pts 75, 150, 225 at 1/25 = 3s, 6s, 9s.

A clip with no scene change produces a HEADER-ONLY object: the `#...` header lines and the `#stream#, dts, pts, ...` column line, and zero data rows. The job still exits 0 and uploads the object (218 bytes here). ADR-027 D3's zero-cut rule can rely on this.

Object location: exactly the dest key given in cmdLineArgs. The job applies no lifecycle or expiry; the object persists until something deletes it. The platform's job removal (`removeJob`) does not remove it.

The object is the only place the cuts appear. The log of an exit-0 job holds only the wrapper's own lines (`Running ffmpeg with command`, `Generating signed URL for S3 input`, `Output file`, `Staging directory`, `Actual command string`, `cmdString`, `Uploaded ...`); no `showinfo` or `pts_time` lines.

SECURITY NOTE: the job log contains the presigned input URL in full, including `X-Amz-Signature`, valid for `X-Amz-Expires=21600` (6 hours), twice (`Actual command string` and `cmdString`). Anyone who can read the log can fetch the source for 6 hours. The logs above are redacted. Callers that retain or forward job logs (src/pipeline/osc-job-log.ts) should redact `X-Amz-Signature` and `X-Amz-Credential` first.
Test inputs were generated locally and the test objects were deleted after the run; the job instances were removed with `removeJob`.

Does the job log truncate or page on a long video, and at what size?

Does /logs/:name return the container's stderr stream as well as stdout? (The repo records the probe parse working in production, which implies yes for console.error, but no capture is recorded here.)
ANSWERED 2026-10-28: yes. The framemd5-to-S3 shape completes, exits 0 and uploads; see `sceneCutReadback.viaS3Object.liveRun`.
